h: Wine and Mercy at the Three Shabbos Meals

p: עַל דָּא מַאן דְּחָמֵי יַיִן וְכוּלֵּי
"Therefore one who sees wine in a dream, etc.:
if he is a talmid chacham,
'And wine gladdens the heart of man,'
'For your love is better than wine';
and this is the preserved wine,
to offer these things in the offering,
that the wine of the libations
and it removes the wine of judgment,
which is the wine "for those bitter of soul."
that in the three Shabbos meals,
is from the aspect of Eden;
for Shabbos is a semblance of Olam HaBa;
and it says in the Gemara (Berachos 34b):
this is the wine preserved in its grapes,
of any creature has had dominion," etc.
the wine preserved in its grapes.
at the first two Shabbos meals
in the holy Zohar cited above:
For the meal of Shabbos night
of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which is that of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
whose attribute is kindness and love
nevertheless we find in the Midrash
there was in him also the attribute of zealotry,
who acts against the will of Hashem Yisbarach.
the attribute of kindness and love,
he wanted to clarify about himself
that it was not merely because
he was born so by nature;
for there is one who is good by nature
to be zealous and take vengeance
against the will of Hashem Yisbarach.
And this is called a zealot:
like Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
who was not obligated to pursue,
against four kings and their armies;
and especially according to the view
only because there burned in him
and as they expounded about them in the Midrash
because of this he was zealous
for the law that "zealots strike him"
was not given over to the beis din;
that if Zimri had separated, etc.,
he is not executed for him."
even for the transgressors and the guilty;
for the episode of the Calf:
'your God' in the plural is not said," etc.;
except in what was said to him explicitly,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר שָׁם בָּעֵגֶל (שְׁמוֹת לב, כז)
as it says there regarding the Calf (Shemos 32:27):
"Thus said Hashem, the God of Yisrael:
שִׂימוּ אִישׁ חַרְבּוֹ עַל יְרֵכוֹ וְגוֹ׳
put every man his sword upon his thigh," etc.,
but in what was not said explicitly
Had we been in the Sanhedrin,
no person would ever have been executed."
And even Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
by this there would be still more
to plead merit for an adulterer, etc.,
as it says in the Gemara (there),
to that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
And therefore he said to Pinchas:
since zeal for Hashem burns in you,
the matter befits you and is fitting for you;

p: And this is the matter of
how to declare the sheretz pure," etc.;
so that he can plead merit
for it says in the Gemara (Taanis 16a):
To a person who holds a sheretz in his hand,
who even if he immerses," etc.
And this one has the power
for one who immerses with a sheretz in his hand,
for in the end it will enter his heart
also had in him the attribute of zealotry.
And this is what it says in the Midrash
who were called fearers of God:
הָיָה בּוֹ מִדַּת הַיִּרְאָה גַּם כֵּן
he also had the attribute of fear,
Therefore, also at the morning meal,
of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
as is written in the holy Zohar cited above.
"in which is the Will of Wills,
there is no need at all
And also, since it is the meal
and it says in the Tikkunim
and that one from the soul";
an aspect only of pleading merit,
and his attribute is the attribute of mercy,
will not be lost, chas v'shalom;
And similar to this it says
the reason they did not institute
and it is similar to what we said.
that the Arizal would drink wine
but here it is after eating,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ה, א)
in the manner of what it says (Shir HaShirim 5:1):
And it appears that by this reason
for the main thing is the drinking,
for its essence is the allusion
to the wine of the Torah
is likened to all the drinks
and the well, which is water,
הָיָה בּוֹ טַעַם כָּל הַמַּשְׁקִים גַּם כֵּן
there was the taste of all drinks as well,
as it says in the Mechilta.

paragraphs.text: Source: Shir HaShirim 5:1 — “באתי לגני אחתי כלה אריתי מורי עם בשמי אכלתי יערי עם דבשי שתיתי ייני עם חלבי אכלו רעים שתו ושכרו דודים” — “I have come to my garden, My own, my bride;I have plucked my myrrh and spice, Eaten my honey and honeycomb, Drunk my wine and my milk.
